issues.issue: The two sentences are inconsistent: the Company will be structured "so as not to subject" itself to the Investment Company Act, yet "[i]n the alternative" expects to rely on the Section 3(c)(5) exemption from registration under that same Act.
The provision speaks of not subjecting "the Fund" to the Act, a term the Memorandum never defines; the issuer is defined throughout as "the Company".

The suggestion that "the Noteholders may be deemed lenders with respect to the Notes" sits against the Tax section's position that the Notes are indebtedness and against the Executive Summary's characterisation of Noteholders as secured creditors.

The acknowledgment that interest paid to Noteholders "may exceed the applicable statutorily-defined usury rates" sits against the Note Terms, which fix a Floating Rate with an 8% minimum below the 10% California threshold identified here.
"[C]ommercially reasonable efforts" and "as advisable ... where appropriate" state no measurable compliance obligation.
The passage refers to "the inability of the Portfolio Manager to repay such Loan", using a term that appears nowhere else and evidently means the Portfolio Borrower.
The paragraph shifts to "the Project Owner", a term used nowhere else in the Memorandum, where the party meant is the Portfolio Borrower.

The sentence "the Company ... may be limited by law or by the terms of its loan agreement, including without limitation with respect to the following" is incomplete and refers to an unidentified "loan agreement".

The statement that the Company only "intends to require" adequate insurance is weaker than the Escrow Conditions, under which no funds may be disbursed until satisfactory fire and casualty insurance naming the Company as loss payee has been obtained.
The paragraph uses "Other Sponsored Funds", a label the Memorandum never defines; Section III defines only "Other Sponsored Investment Funds".

Foreclosing on a pledge of equity in a Portfolio Borrower would make the Company an owner and operator of the borrower, which sits against "Sale of Loans Generally", stating the Company does not expect to engage in real estate operations, and against the stated Company Purpose.

The statement that the Manager and its members "will receive Company gains" disproportionate to their capital contribution is difficult to square with "Manager's and Affiliate Member's Investment" and with the fixed fee structure in "Manager Compensation", which provides no gain-sharing.
Describing the purchase of Notes as subject to risks "typical of investments in private equity funds" sits against the repeated characterisation of Noteholders as creditors holding debt, not equity.

The flat statement that the Company "has no operating history" and that past performance "cannot be relied upon" points the other way from the Executive Summary and Section II claims of a "proven lending record" and a "100% collection record".

The acknowledgment that the portfolio "may become concentrated in a limited number of portfolio loans" is in tension with "Loan Diversification", which caps any single new loan commitment at 20% of Company capital after the second year.

The warning that the Noteholders' security interest may not even "be perfected in seniority over the interests of other creditors" cannot be squared with the Executive Summary's flat statement that "[t]he Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company" and that Noteholders "will be secured creditors".

The statement that the structure "precludes the Noteholders ... from voting on Company operating matters" conflicts with "Restricted Actions" and "Amendments, Waivers of Noteholder Agreements", which give a Majority in Interest of Noteholders approval rights over mergers, liens, salaries and amendments.

This provision abbreviates the Investment Company Act of 1940 as "the Company Act", while the cover page defines the same statute as the "Investment Company Act" and Section VIII calls it the "Companies Act" — three labels for one statute.

The provision conditions additional subscriptions on meeting standards at the time of an "Interest Roll-over Request", a capitalised term never defined; the Note Terms define only "Roll-over Interest".

Clause (iii) refers to an investment company registered under "the United States Companies Act of 1940", a statute that does not exist; the Act meant is the Investment Company Act of 1940, defined differently elsewhere in the Memorandum.

The enumerated accredited-investor categories are narrower than Rule 501 (for example, trusts are limited to IRREVOCABLE TRUSTS), yet the opening words purport to define "Accredited Investor" "within the meaning of Rule 501".

This paragraph contemplates an entity "formed for the purpose of purchasing a Note", whereas clause 1(v) qualifies entities only if "not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note"; the two paragraphs treat the same investor differently.

"[W]ithout unreasonable effort or expense" limits the information undertaking by an unmeasured standard, and "necessary to verify the accuracy of the information furnished" leaves the scope of what must be produced open.

The Memorandum is said to outline the structure of the Company "and its Managing Member", a role never defined here; the operative provisions vest management in the "Manager" and describe the Principals as "Managing Directors".
